question.text: Indravati Growth Capital (Cat II) is planning to raise INR 500 crore across domestic HNIs, family offices and an offshore SWF anchor. The manager is evaluating Placement Agents and Distributors. Which statement BEST captures their role?

answer.text: Placement agents replace SEBI-registered merchant bankers for PPM filing
Placement agents are only required for offshore feeder structures

Placement agents and distributors are important for SELLING units AND for creating wider awareness/familiarity with AIF products among investors; a distributor can be empanelled with more than one AIF and can be individuals or institutions (distribution companies, broking firms, banks)
Placement agents are SEBI-registered trustees of the AIF

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the chapter, placement agents and distributors play a key role in selling AIF units AND in creating wider awareness and familiarity with AIF products, services, investment strategies, and return potential. A distributor can be empanelled with more than one AIF. Distributors can be individuals or institutions such as distribution companies, broking companies and banks. AIF product distribution requires proper training given the sophisticated/high-risk nature of the products. **The Trap:** The MB-replacement option confuses placement agents with merchant bankers. The offshore-only option over-restricts placement-agent scope. The trustee option confuses roles entirely. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers distributor role. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) is literally the exam for this distributor community — XIX-D tests the Manager's end of the relationship. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Placement agent fees (typically 1-3% of commitments raised) are usually borne by the Manager (out of management fee income), NOT charged to LPs. Disclose the fee quantum transparently in the PPM. Use tiered placement fee grids (lower % for large anchor LPs) to preserve GP economics.
